I didn't have __times to watch__ the whole movie.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** "time to watch".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence** "I didn't have times to watch the whole movie",** the use of **"times"** is incorrect.
 
• The **correct term **to use here is **"time"**, which refers to the indefinite continued progress of existence and events in the past, present, and future regarded as a whole.
 
• The term **"time"** in this context refers to a period of time or an opportunity to do something.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is:* 'I didn't have **time to watch** the whole movie.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect due to the following reasons:

 
 
• **Option 2: "timer to watched" **- The word "timer" refers to a device for measuring time, and it does not fit in this context. The verb form **"watched"** is also **incorrect **as it's in the past tense and does not correctly match with "to", which requires the base form of the verb.
 
• **Option 3: "time to watching"** - This is grammatically incorrect because after the word **"to"**, the base form of the verb should be used. So "watching" should be** "watch".**

• But** 'most' **is something which is not the whole, after it **'of'** is always needed to express the **relationship**.
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• ***Most of** you are eligible.*
 
• ***All of** you are eligible (or) **All** are eligible.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 4.

 ​**

questions.question:

__Tons of sheep__ was grazing in the field.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**A flock of sheep**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the **common noun plural form** 'Tons' is incorrect.
 
• The verb 'was' in the given sentence is a singular verb.
 
• We know that a singular subject will always take a singular verb.
 
• Therefore, the **singular common noun** 'A flock' should be used in place of 'Tons'.

Correct Sentence__: ***A flock of sheep** was grazing in the field*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural).
 
• Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is a plural, its verb must also be plural.
 
• Some animal group names:
 
 
• *A **school **of fish*
 
• *A **herd **of rabbits*
 
• *A **zeal **of zebras*
 
• *A **leap **of leopards*

His words wield tremendous influence **__between his followers.__**
questions.solution:

__
 
• The preposition** "between" **is used when referring to two entities.
 
• When referring to more than two entities,** "among"** is used.
 
• So, the** correct phrase** is "among his followers."

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *His words wield tremendous influence **among** his followers.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Within**: "Within" refers to something that is contained or exists inside a particular boundary or limits.
 
• **In: **"In" indicates being inside or within the boundaries of something.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.**

Mahatma Gandhi is undoubtedly one of the __much__ popular authors of our times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **most**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace '**much'** with '**most'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **'Most'** denotes the greatest or highest degree, often used with an adjective or adverb to form the **superlative**. 
 
 
• **Example - ***Peter is one of the **most** reliable people on this planet.*
 
 
 
• **Superlative** adjectives are used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of quality.
 
• The **comparative** form of '**much'** is** 'more'**, and the **superlative** form of '**much' **is the '**most'.**
 
• **'Much' **means a large amount, while **'most'** means the largest amount in comparison with other things.
 
 
• **Example - ***I will lend you as **much** money as you want.*
 
 
 
• **'One of the'** is always used with **superlatives** and it is used when we are referring to someone or something specific among many others.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Corrected sentence:** *Mahatma Gandhi is undoubtedly one of the **most** popular authors of our times. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Best** means the most excellent or desirable type or quality.
 
• **Total** means the whole number or amount of something.
 
• **Better **describes something as being superior or is an adverb that means something is done to a higher degree or more completely.

• **"Than"** is used to introduce the second event that happened immediately after the first event.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

I was waiting __from__ two hours.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**for**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of the **preposition **"**from**" is incorrect.
 
• We use the **preposition** '**from' **to show where **something starts or originates**. We also use **from** to show movement from one thing to another.
 
• In the given sentence, we need to use the preposition "**for**".
 
• We use the preposition 'for' to state how long something lasts or continues.
 
 
• **Example**: *I waited at the metro station **for **__about 45 minutes so that I could catch the first metro.*
 
 
 
• We also use the preposition "**for**" as a conjunction to link the** first and second clauses of a sentence**.
 
• The implied meaning of the given sentence is that the speaker is expressing how long they waited.

**The correct sentence is**: *I was waiting **__for__**** **two hours.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the following sentence.**

I am trying to study, __if it is impossible__ with all this noise.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**but it is impossible**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence expresses a contrast between the speaker's desire to study and the distracting noise.
 
• '**But**' expresses this contrast and maintains the original meaning.
 
• The conjunction "**but**" is used to indicate a contrast or contradiction between the two clauses.
 
• In this case, the first part of the sentence expresses the effort to study, and the second part introduces the obstacle (noise) that makes studying impossible.
 
• Using "**but**" clarifies the relationship between these contrasting elements, resulting in a more coherent and grammatically correct sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**If**': Used to introduce a condition or a possibility.
 
• '**That**': Often used to introduce a clause, provide additional information, or indicate a consequence.
 
• '**While**': Used to indicate a contrast or simultaneous occurrence.
 
• '**Unless**': Indicates a condition that must be met for a certain outcome to happen.

**An ultralight airplane is very different from a conventional airplane. It __is looking like__ a lawn chair with wings.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• But the correct verb form to use in this sentence is '**looks like**' which is in the simple present tense and describes a general truth or fact.
 
• The use of '**like**' after the verb '**looks**' is correct because it indicates a comparison between the ultralight airplane and a lawn chair with wings.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.**

The new restaurant is __more better__ than the old one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Better**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of "more" before "better" is incorrect as "**better**" is already a comparative form of the adjective "**good**".
 
• The correct comparative form of "**good**" is "**better**", and the superlative form is "**the best**".
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence should be "*The new restaurant is better than the old one.*"

Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The comparative and superlative forms of adjectives are used to compare and describe different degrees of a particular quality.
 
• 
 
**Comparative Form**:

 
 
• 
 
**Usage**: The comparative form is used when you are comparing two things or two groups.

 
 
• 
 
**Formation**: Most adjectives form the comparative by adding "-er" (e.g., faster, taller) or by using "more" before the adjective (e.g., more beautiful, more interesting).

 
 
• 
 
**Example**: The cat is faster than the dog.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Superlative Form**:

 
 
• 
 
**Usage**: The superlative form is used when you are comparing more than two things or groups, indicating the highest degree of quality.

 
 
• 
 
**Formation**: Most adjectives form the superlative by adding "-est" (e.g., fastest, tallest) or by using "most" before the adjective (e.g., most beautiful, most interesting).

 
 
• 
 
**Example**: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The early morning flight is the **__lest expensive.__**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct improvement **for the sentence *"The early morning flight is the 'lest expensive.'" would be "The early morning flight is the 'least expensive.'"*
 
• The **correct word **is** "least", not "lest"**. **"Least"** is used as a superlative degree of little, and it means the smallest amount or degree.
 
• **In this context**, it's used to express that the early morning flight is the cheapest among all options.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'The early morning flight is the least expensive.'*
